gaps.sentence: The suspect is believed ___ the country weeks ago.
gaps.explanation: Believe + to-infinitive; 'weeks ago' demands the perfect infinitive to have left.

gaps.sentence: The whole street ___ when the gas main burst.
gaps.explanation: The street was evacuated by others: past necessity had to be + evacuated.

gaps.sentence: By this time tomorrow, the results ___ to every candidate.
gaps.explanation: 'By this time tomorrow' requires future perfect passive: will have been + emailed.

gaps.sentence: Over two hundred bird species ___ (record) in the valley this spring.
gaps.explanation: 'This spring' is an open time frame, so present perfect passive: have been + recorded.

gaps.sentence: Too much time ___ (waste) on pointless meetings these days.
gaps.explanation: 'These days' signals a present general situation: is + wasted (singular 'time').

gaps.sentence: Did you have the brakes ___ (check) before the long drive?
gaps.hint: question form of have something done
gaps.explanation: Causative question: Did you have + the brakes + checked? A mechanic did the checking.

gaps.sentence: The invitation ___ (send) to the wrong address — nobody on this street received one.
gaps.explanation: Perfect modal passive: must have been + sent. The evidence forces the conclusion.

gaps.sentence: I must get my passport ___ (renew) before the trip.
gaps.explanation: 'Get + object + past participle': the passport is renewed by an authority, not by me.
